messages:
mira: Quick flag 1: our Next/Edge sample started failing on Vercel after switching the mono-repo to pnpm + isolated linker. Node build is fine but edge build errors out with missing export for './runtime/edge'.

mira: Error: Package \"@redwood/sdk\" has no export named \"./runtime/edge\" — package.json clearly has an exports entry. Strange.

joel: That usually smells like a pnpm symlink/hoist problem. When node_modules is a symlink to the package, some bundlers (especially esbuild used by Vercel) don't honor package exports the same way.

mira: We're on pnpm 8 with default node-linker=isolated. Workspace layout: packages/sdk and apps/web. SDK is a workspace package.

sam: Can you paste the SDK's package.json exports? Common mistake is forgetting the require/import shapes or not listing subpath exports.

mira: Here's the relevant snippet:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./runtime/edge": { "import": "./dist/esm/runtime/edge.js" }
}
```

mira: Consumer does `import { createEdgeHandler } from '@redwood/sdk/runtime/edge'`. Build stack resolves to the actual file path under .pnpm/.../node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm/index.js and then resolution for the subpath fails.

tia: We hit this before. Two straightforward workarounds: 1) use node-linker=hoisted so pnpm flattens and you get normal package boundaries, or 2) add a tiny proxy file at package root that re-exports the runtime entry (e.g., runtime-edge.js) and expose it in package.json so consumers import '@redwood/sdk/runtime-edge'. Both avoid depending on subpath export resolution across symlinks.

joel: Another angle is bundler config. Esbuild/webpack both have settings around resolving package exports and symlinks. Webpack has `resolve.symlinks`, node has `--preserve-symlinks`. Esbuild is a bit rough here. Vercel builder might not run the latest resolver logic.

sam: I reproduced locally: monorepo -> apps/web -> import '@redwood/sdk/runtime/edge' -> `pnpm --filter apps/web run build` fails with esbuild when SDK is symlinked. Re-run pnpm install with `node-linker=hoisted` and the build succeeds.

mira: So hoisted fixes it, but we can't force customers to change their linker. Maybe we should update our example and docs.

tia: Agreed. Adding a root-level proxy file is low friction. Create `packages/sdk/runtime-edge.js` containing `module.exports = require('./dist/cjs/runtime/edge.js')` and an ESM shim `export * from './dist/esm/runtime/edge.js'` if needed. Then add "./runtime-edge": "./runtime-edge.js" to exports. Consumers can `import '@redwood/sdk/runtime-edge'` and avoid subpath export lookup issues.

alex: Also consider adding a note to devex: list known workspace managers (pnpm, yarn, turborepo) and the recommended CI matrix: build example with `node-linker=isolated` and `node-linker=hoisted`. Add a test that runs `pnpm install` with both modes so we catch regressions.

sam: Troubleshooting steps to reproduce I used locally: 

```bash
# from monorepo root
pnpm i
cd apps/web
# try build to see the esbuild resolution error
pnpm run build
# quick diagnostic to see where the package.json is resolved
node -e "console.log(require.resolve('@redwood/sdk/package.json'))"
# try alternate linker
echo 'node-linker=hoisted' > .npmrc
pnpm i --force
pnpm --filter apps/web run build
```

mira: I opened a tiny PR against examples to switch the Next/Edge sample import to `@redwood/sdk/runtime-edge` and added a note in the sample README about pnpm symlink caveats: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/81 (WIP).

ci-bot: CI preview built the example with default pnpm settings and with hoisted mode; both builds passed on the preview run. :white_check_mark:

joel: Nice. For longer term: we should decide whether to keep maintaining the root proxy file or find a bundler-compatible solution. Proxy file is simplest and has negligible maintenance cost.

tia: Also add a small section in SDK docs for "common monorepo build issues" that includes: exports visibility, preserveSymlinks flags, and recommended imports.

mira: I'll file a follow-up issue to add CI coverage and docs. Thanks everyone! :pray:
